classification_note: The saved crash is a MemorySanitizer use-of-uninitialized-value because the consumed-byte overcount makes the second MMR decode read the uninitialized tail of an over-allocated heap buffer. The underlying logical bug is the first-plane refill bookkeeping error and the resulting unsigned size underflow at the next plane decode.

bug_description.original: The MMR decoder in jbig2dec pre-buffers up to 32 bits of encoded input data in a word buffer before consumption. When refilling the buffer, the decoder avoids reading data from succeeding segments but still reports having consumed those bytes, even though they were never read. After finishing, the MMR decoder propagates an incorrect number of consumed bytes to the caller. The caller then subtracts this incorrect value from the size, leading to an underflow. This causes subsequent MMR decoding to read input data from the wrong location and eventually attempt to read outside the MMR encoded input buffer.
bug_description.normalized: The staged 410-byte JBIG2 witness is copied into `jbig2_data_in`'s heap buffer `ctx->buf`; because the initial allocation loop doubles `initial_buf_size` once before testing, that first copy lands in a 2048-byte allocation whose trailing bytes remain uninitialized. The file reaches a halftone region whose parsed flags set `HMMR = 1`, so gray-scale decoding uses `jbig2_decode_halftone_mmr`. In the first bitplane decode, vulnerable `jbig2_decode_mmr_consume` advances `mmr->data_index` for every consumed byte even after `mmr->data_index + 4 >= mmr->size` and no replacement byte is read, so `jbig2_decode_halftone_mmr` returns a `consumed_bytes` count larger than the actual first-plane payload. The next bitplane call at `jbig2_decode_gray_scale_image:340` then computes `data + consumed_bytes` and `size - consumed_bytes` without checking `consumed_bytes <= size`, advancing the data pointer beyond the valid MMR payload and underflowing the unsigned size. In that second MMR decode, the refill path in `jbig2_decode_mmr_consume` treats bytes past the logical payload as available and ORs uninitialized tail bytes from `ctx->buf` into `mmr->word`. `jbig2_decode_mmr_line` then dispatches on that poisoned `word` and MemorySanitizer reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` at `jbig2_mmr.c:950:18`.

source.description: First project-code statement that consumes the fuzz buffer on the vulnerable path. It copies the staged JBIG2 file into decoder heap buffer `ctx->buf`, creating the initialized prefix and preserving the uninitialized tail that the later over-advanced MMR pointer reaches.
source.value_from: The libFuzzer harness passes the staged `poc` bytes directly to `jbig2_data_in` (`jbig2_fuzzer.cc:107`). The saved witness file is exactly 410 bytes long. On this first call, the preceding `do { buf_size <<= 1; } while (buf_size < size);` grows `initial_buf_size` from 1024 to 2048 before the copy, so only the first 410 bytes of `ctx->buf` are initialized by the PoC.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: MSAN crash site. In the second `jbig2_decode_halftone_mmr` call reached from `jbig2_decode_gray_scale_image:340`, local `word` contains bits refilled from the wrong, over-advanced input pointer, and this branch dispatch is the first observed use of the uninitialized value.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `jbig2_mmr.c:950:18` with callers `jbig2_decode_halftone_mmr`, `jbig2_decode_gray_scale_image:340`, `jbig2_decode_halftone_region:506`, and `jbig2_halftone_region:629`.

root_cause.description: This increment executes for every eight consumed bits even when the preceding `if (mmr->data_index + 4 < mmr->size)` skipped the refill read. The first MMR plane therefore counts unread bytes as consumed, which corrupts the returned `consumed_bytes` and sets up the later pointer/size underflow.
root_cause.note: The fix introduces explicit `consumed_bits`, bounds refills with `mmr->data_index < mmr->size`, and computes returned bytes from `consumed_bits` instead of the old `data_index`/`bit_index` approximation.

tainted_value_origin.description: This line turns the corrupted first-plane MMR context state into the caller-visible `consumed_bytes` value used in `data + consumed_bytes` and `size - consumed_bytes` at the next bitplane decode.

parser_admitted.description: After file-header and segment-header parsing, the selected segment type dispatches into the halftone-region parser. This is the parser-path admission point for the vulnerable halftone/MMR decoding chain.

fine_trace.note: Copies the exact 410-byte PoC into decoder buffer `ctx->buf`. Because the earlier `do { buf_size <<= 1; } while (buf_size < size);` runs once before checking, the first call allocated 2048 bytes at line 229, so this step initializes only the prefix `[0, 410)` and leaves the tail `[410, 2048)` as uninitialized heap state.
Reads the halftone-region flags from the attacker-controlled segment body and sets `params.HMMR = 1`, selecting MMR-coded gray-scale decoding instead of the arithmetic path.

fine_trace.code: code = jbig2_decode_halftone_region(ctx, segment, &params, segment_data + offset, segment->data_length - offset, image, GB_stats);
fine_trace.note: After parsing 38 bytes of halftone-region header, the decoder treats the remaining segment bytes as the gray-scale payload and hands both the payload pointer and its size to the inner halftone decoder. The already-parsed `params.HMMR = 1` accompanies that payload into the MMR path.

Derives the number of gray-scale bitplanes from the referred pattern dictionary. The saved crash stack later reports execution at `jbig2_decode_gray_scale_image:340`, so for this witness the computed `HBPP` must be greater than 1; otherwise the second-plane MMR call would never execute.

On the first `jbig2_decode_halftone_mmr` invocation (the `GSPLANES[GSBPP - 1]` decode at `jbig2_decode_gray_scale_image:312`), initializes the MMR context from the original halftone payload and prebuffers up to the first four bytes into `mmr->word`. `consumed_bytes` is still 0 on this first plane.

During first-plane decoding, once the prebuffer nears the true end of the MMR payload, the refill `if` stops reading bytes from input but `mmr->data_index++` still runs for each consumed byte. The context therefore counts unread bytes as consumed. This is the bookkeeping bug addressed by the fix's `consumed_bits` rewrite.

When the first plane returns, this formula converts the corrupted MMR state from step 6 into the caller-visible `consumed_bytes` value. Because unread bytes were already counted as consumed, the returned byte count is larger than the actual first-plane MMR payload.

fine_trace.var: data + consumed_bytes, size - consumed_bytes, consumed_bytes, j
fine_trace.code: code = jbig2_decode_halftone_mmr(ctx, &rparams, data + consumed_bytes, size - consumed_bytes, GSPLANES[j], &consumed_bytes);
fine_trace.note: On the next loop iteration, the decoder reuses the same base payload but does not check `consumed_bytes <= size` before computing `data + consumed_bytes` and `size - consumed_bytes`. The inflated count from step 7 therefore advances the pointer beyond the valid MMR payload and underflows the unsigned size passed to the second `jbig2_decode_halftone_mmr`. The saved crash stack naming `jbig2_decode_gray_scale_image:340` is direct runtime evidence that this second-plane call executed.

In the second `jbig2_decode_halftone_mmr` call from step 8, the underflowed `mmr->size` makes the refill test treat bytes beyond the logical MMR payload as available. The OR at line 87 can therefore pull bytes from the over-advanced pointer into the uninitialized tail of `ctx->buf` and fold them into `mmr->word`. The saved MSan origin frames explicitly name lines 82 and 87 in this function.

At the top of the decode loop, line 858 copies `mmr->word` into local `word`; after step 9 that scalar contains uninitialized bits from the wrong refill source. This branch dispatch is the first reported use of that poisoned value, so MemorySanitizer aborts here with `use-of-uninitialized-value`.

allocation_context.note: MSAN says the uninitialized value was created by the heap allocation that backs `ctx->buf`. `jbig2_data_in` allocates that buffer here and later initializes only the 410-byte PoC prefix with `memcpy`, leaving the rest of the 2048-byte allocation undefined.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Partial — MSAN's origin is the over-allocated `ctx->buf` heap allocation, while the logical bug is the earlier first-plane refill bookkeeping that makes the second-plane decode read from that uninitialized tail.

format.name: JBIG2 document
format.contract: The staged witness is the exact 410-byte JBIG2 file in `poc`, beginning with the standard JBIG2 header bytes `97 4a 42 32 0d 0a 1a 0a`. The source-grounded trigger proven here is only that this file reaches a halftone region whose parsed flags set `HMMR = 1`, the referred pattern dictionary yields more than one gray-scale bitplane (`HBPP > 1`, as shown by the saved stack at `jbig2_decode_gray_scale_image:340`), the first `jbig2_decode_halftone_mmr` call overstates `consumed_bytes`, and the next bitplane decode therefore executes `data + consumed_bytes` / `size - consumed_bytes` on the same heap buffer and later consumes uninitialized tail bytes. The staged artifacts do not establish the exact numeric `HBPP`, `HNUMPATS`, or `consumed_bytes` values for this witness or justify a broader trigger class than files reproducing this same second-plane underflow relation.
